answer.generated: Concurrency is fundamental to OS design because it addresses core issues such as communication among processes, sharing of resources like memory and I/O, synchronization of multiple activities, and allocation of processor time. These problems arise when many processes execute simultaneously, requiring mechanisms to coordinate their interactions efficiently. Without proper handling, concurrency can lead to deadlocks, race conditions, and performance degradation, making it essential for any operating system that supports multitasking.
